notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 01/21/2026
Patient: Alison Homenick, 66-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 01/21/2026. The study was conducted to assess sleep patterns and identify any sleep-disordered breathing events. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 26.4 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 2% of all events. Sleep architecture showed normal distribution of sleep stages with no significant abnormalities. The findings indicate moderate obstructive sleep apnea with a small proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical correlation and appropriate management are recommended.

notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/01/2026
Patient: Alison Homenick, 66-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of ongoing sleep apnea symptoms despite CPAP therapy.

History:
Ms. Homenick has been using CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. She reports consistent nightly use of the device.

Findings:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 29.1 events/hour on CPAP at 14 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates significant residual apnea-hypopnea events despite adherence to CPAP therapy at a pressure of 14 cmH2O. This indicates suboptimal control of her sleep apnea.

Plan:
1. Consider alternative treatment options including bilevel positive airway pressure or advanced PAP modalities.
2. Re-evaluate mask fit and compliance.
3. Schedule follow-up sleep study to assess efficacy of any therapy adjustments.
4. Continue monitoring symptoms and adherence.

Summary:
Ms. Homenick's current CPAP therapy is insufficient to control her sleep apnea as evidenced by a residual AHI of 29.1 events/hour. Further evaluation and treatment modification are warranted.
